title: prune_reopened_refs judges a gone item file against the integration main, not the checkout it runs in
goal: Found by the fresh-context review of SP-matmvkn6, item ST-ihtjygip (Sprint close and drop delete the refs/kb-reopened ref of each item they remove): refs/kb-reopened/* is shared by every worktree of a clone, but prune_reopened_refs judges an item file gone by the checkout the command runs in, so a drop outside a sprint run in an older worktree deletes the reopen ref of a live item filed on main after that worktree branched. The prune deletes a ref only when the item file is absent from the integration main tree too (origin/main), and a ref of an item that exists there is kept. No test names kb-reopened or prune_reopened_refs, so removing the call in cmd_close (_tools/bl_land.py) or cmd_drop (_tools/bl_items.py) passes every gate: one planted-failure test in _tools/test_land_e2e.py, within the ceiling in _tools/tests_ceiling.json, runs close or drop in an isolated git repo and asserts a removed item's ref is gone, a live item's ref (also one filed on main after the checkout branched) kept, and a drop inside a sprint prunes nothing.

gates.question: What does prune_reopened_refs do when the integration main tree cannot be read (no origin/main in the clone)?
options: keep every reopen ref and prune nothing
judge by the checkout's backlog directory alone, as today
gates.recommendation: keep every reopen ref and prune nothing
gates.answer: keep every reopen ref and prune nothing
